source.title: Liu Chuanzhi, 'godfather' of Chinese PC industry, retires as chairman of Legend Holdings

passages.text: Liu and ten other researchers received a 200,000-yuan investment from the Institute of Computing Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1984 to set up ICT New Technology Development Company, the predecessor of Legend and later Lenovo, starting in an office space under 20 square meters.
Founded ICT New Technology Development Company (later Legend, then Lenovo) in 1984 using a state-institute investment.
Retired as Chairman of Legend Holdings in December 2019, handing the role to CFO Ning Min while retaining honorary chairman, senior adviser, and strategy-committee positions.

Ning Min succeeded Liu as Legend Holdings chairman in December 2019; Liu remained honorary chairman, senior adviser, and a member of the board's strategy committee, per SCMP's report on the exchange filing.

source.title: Lenovo CEO Yang Yuanqing Adds Chairman Role as Founder Liu Chuanzhi Turns Focus to New Challenges

passages.text: Liu returned as Lenovo chairman in February 2009 to help lead a turnaround after the 2008-09 global economic downturn hurt the company's results.

Liu Chuanzhi expressed confidence that Lenovo had established a durable global culture of commitment and ownership across its workforce, framing the company's post-acquisition integration of IBM's personal-computer business as culturally consolidated.
Returned to the Lenovo chairmanship in February 2009 during the global financial crisis to steer a turnaround.
Lenovo achieved a successful turnaround under Liu and Yang Yuanqing, regaining momentum in the PC market and expanding into mobile internet, per Lenovo's own 2011 press release.

Liu Chuanzhi — founder profiled in the Chinese Founder Ledger — is documented as follows: institute of Computing Technology researcher who in 1984 used a 200,000-yuan state-institute investment to found what became Legend/Lenovo, later engineering Lenovo's 2004 acquisition of IBM's PC business before retiring from Legend Holdings' chairmanship in December 2019. The profile is grounded in the 2 sources indexed for this founder.

Liu Chuanzhi's role is documented as: founder of Legend (later Lenovo); retired as Chairman of Legend Holdings in 2019, retaining honorary chairman, senior adviser, and strategy-committee roles Retired as Chairman of Legend Holdings as of December 2019, per South China Morning Post reporting on the Hong Kong stock exchange filing; retained honorary chairman/adviser roles at that date (research date: 2026-08-23).

Liu-chuanzhi belongs to Group 2 - Reform-era pioneers. The reform-era pioneers group covers founders who built their businesses in the 1980s and 1990s opening of China's economy under Deng Xiaoping, spanning telecom equipment (Huawei), personal computing (Lenovo), home appliances (Haier), beverages (Wahaha), and automotive components (Wanxiang), often starting from township-enterprise or small-collective origins.
